subject: LedgerCorp reserved throughput drift — exec brief and next steps
messages:
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@ledgercorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@ledgercorp.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Sudden throughput drop on reserved pool (production)

Irene — we started seeing a drop in successful requests served from our reserved capacity around 10:30 ET. Latency climbed from ~90ms p50 to ~700ms and error rates (5xx) are at ~3.2% for the last 20 minutes. No config changes on our side; there was a spike in inference QPS this morning but within our committed window. Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side and what the immediate mitigation will be?

We rely on the dedicated pool for critical checkout scoring — this is impacting orders.

Sara
VP Engineering, LedgerCorp

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on reserved pool (production)

Sara — thanks for the flag and the data. We're pulling an ops bridge right now (network and serving teams). Initial telemetry shows a sustained queue depth increase on LedgerCorp's dedicated pool and an elevated KV-cache miss rate after a model rollout earlier this morning. We're treating this as highest priority.

Immediate next steps: 
- I've asked infra to attach additional headroom from our burst buffer (10gPU-minutes) while we triage (ETA ~8m).
- Priyom and David are running a quick validation on the model variant that rolled at 09:58 ET to check for kernel regressions.
- We'll forward svc traces and a short RCA note within 30 minutes.

I'll keep you updated in this thread and on the bridge.

— Irene
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: svc-trace-logs-05-19.tar.gz (compressed traces)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden throughput drop on reserved pool (production)

Summary of what I see from the runtime: 
- Around 09:58 ET a new model shard variant was activated for LedgerCorp (small quantized variant). Kernel selection changed to an alternate CUDA path that increases per-token overhead at short sequence lengths.
- Queue depth increased as the scheduler attempted to batch requests; auto-batching parameters were unchanged, but effective batch build time rose due to slower tail kernel.
- KV-cache hit ratio dropped by ~18% after the variant switch (likely warm-cache invalidation).

Temporary mitigations I recommend now: 
1) Roll the model variant back to previous kernel (we can flip within 5 minutes) — low-risk and expected to restore latency.
2) Temporarily raise per-customer concurrency cap on the dedicated pool from 32 -> 48 and enable fast-path batching bypass for short sequences to reduce batching latency.

If leadership wants the safer, fastest path: rollback + burst headroom. I'll stand by to execute.

— David
SR Engineer, Serving Runtime

Marissa — we need exec awareness. LedgerCorp is a priority reserved customer (DEAL-8791). David's findings suggest a model-variant rollout precipitated the headroom squeeze and higher error rates. Proposed immediate actions: 
- Approve model rollback + activate burst buffer (combined expected to restore service in ~7–10 minutes).
- If we see continued tail risk after rollback, request a short SLA exception to allow temporary capacity bump while we re-evaluate kernel selection and quantization profile (target: <72 hours).

Please advise — if you approve, I'll notify Sara and execute with Priyom and David.

— Irene
